message.content:
You are a COMPLETENESS reader in a verification cycle (Q-61). You work from the PRIMARY TRANSCRIPTS ONLY — you must NOT read the write-up you are auditing (the DNA evidence file), so that what you list is independent of it. Your final text is raw data for an orchestrator. Do not edit any file.

PRIMARY ARTIFACTS (Rev machine transcripts, State of Utah v. Tyler James Robinson, Case 251403576):
1. ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/prelim-hearing-transcripts/day5.txt (~108k chars) — READ END TO END the testimony of ATF analyst OLIVER (roughly lines 600–2703; locate and declare the exact range) and skim the rest for DNA content.
2. ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/prelim-hearing-transcripts/day4.txt (~313k chars) — DO NOT read end to end; grep only, for DNA-relevant passages (patterns: DNA, likelihood, ratio, contributor, swab, elimination, biology, Dremel, toolmark AND DNA co-occurrence; declare patterns + hit counts) and read the hit neighborhoods.

Validate search method first: run `./tsearch.py --validate` from ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research and quote the result before relying on any search null.

TASK: produce the list of MATERIAL facts, caveats, limits, numbers, and null statements in this testimony that a library file titled "DNA evidence — what it can bear" MUST record to be faithful. Pay particular attention to: activity-level disclaimers (what the testing CAN and CANNOT speak to), secondary/indirect transfer testimony, consumption of samples, item designators (note: "Oliver NNN" display designators are NOT exhibit numbers; the FBI and ATF do NOT share an item-numbering series — never write a bare "7.1"/"8.1"), the isoallele exchanges, and anything a party tried to elicit that the witness refused or qualified.

For each item:
- id: C2-nn
- locator: file + line number(s) + Rev timestamp string
- content: fact/caveat/limit with short verbatim quote (≤40 words)
- materiality: what a reader would get WRONG if this is omitted or misstated; if "nothing material," DROP it — strict gate.

HAZARDS: (9) Rev speaker labels are NOT evidence — on Day 5 specifically, a party's advocate's argument can carry the OPPOSING party's counsel label, and a witness answer carries defence counsel's label at least once; infer every speaker from content and never resolve a label to a real person without stated basis. (10) Timestamps are locators; no clock-time conversion; duration measurement across recesses is UNTESTED for Days 3–5 — do not do it.

LIVING-PERSONS RULES: Lance Twiggs was GRANTED use immunity by two offices; his sworn statement was received IN LIEU OF live testimony — never phrase him as having "testified." Elimination-sample donors are NOT suspects; carry the record's non-suspect framing. Tyler Robinson is presumed innocent and has not been bound over. No case-posture statements. Quote minimally.

Output: method declaration (exact ranges read with first/last line quotes, greps + hit counts), then the item list.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
